question: Does satisfying a traffic signal warrant automatically require installation of a traffic control signal?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The MUTCD explicitly states that meeting a signal warrant does not by itself require installing a traffic control signal. Warrant satisfaction is only one factor in an engineering study, and alternatives to signals should be considered even when warrants are met. Standards (mandatory): - "The satisfaction of a traffic signal warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of a traffic control signal." - Similarly, for the parallel case of stop control: "The satisfaction of an all-way stop control warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of all-way stop control at an unsignalized intersection." Guidance (recommended): - Because road user delay and the frequency of some types of crashes are sometimes higher under signal control than under STOP sign control, consideration should be given to providing alternatives to traffic control signals even if one or more signal warrants has been satisfied. - Where volumes must be estimated (e.g., locations under development or construction), a signal installed under projected conditions should have an engineering study done within 1 year of steady (stop-and-go) operation to determine if it is justified; if not justified, the signal should be taken out of steady operation or removed (except where Warrant 8 was used to justify the signal). Support (explanatory): - The safe and efficient movement of all road users is the primary consideration in the engineering study; warrant satisfaction is one relevant factor but is not intended to be the only factor or overriding consideration. Signal installation at an inappropriate location could adversely impact safety, and agencies can even install a signal where no warrants are met if an engineering study documents the rationale. - The Crash Experience warrant illustrates that individual warrants address specific reasons (e.g., crash severity and frequency) for considering a signal, not a mandate to install one. Citations: - Section 4C.01 Standard §3 (p.651) - Section 2B.12 Standard §5 (p.79) - Section 4B.03 Guidance §1 (p.649) - Section 4C.01 Guidance §12 (p.652) - Section 4C.01 Support §20 (p.653) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661)
gold_answer: No. A warrant is a threshold that triggers analysis; it is not conclusive justification. Installation must be based on an engineering study considering safety, operation, alternatives, and the site. A signal can also be installed where no warrant is met if an engineering study documents why it is the best solution.
